title: React kit: sign-in
summary: The React kit's one sign-in form in an Electron window on Windows, labelled as a fixture of DJDL, Polaris look by default with DJDL as the hero: Sign in, offline, Finish in your browser, sign-in that didn't finish, the code view, Choose a license (rows led by their origin), no license on this account, and the toast once signed in, plus what the Electron build writes.
compare: The product is the hero on every step: DJDL's icon and name lead, the accent comes from the icon (coral), and no Polaris Key mark or Powered-by appears; the only Polaris Key words are the footnote's.
With an empty theme the kit draws the Polaris look: Rubik at 400/500/600, filled fields and buttons with no outlines, hairlines only, 10px control radius; theme is the one prop that restyles it.

One form: the window header and art persist, and the icon and title sit at the same offset on every step; each step morphs in place under a header that never moves. No sheet, dialog or popup stacks on it.

Step 1 copy: 'Sign in to DJDL', 'Use the email you bought DJDL with.', primary 'Continue in browser' with an outbound glyph, 'Have a license key?', and the footnote 'Polaris Key signs you in for DJDL. Halcyon Sound never sees your codes or passkeys.' No passkey or device-code row on desktop; no logo row when the product has no provider connections.

Step 2: 'Finish in your browser', the body copy from signin.handoff.browserBody, and a 'Waiting for your browser…' status row as the focus: accent-tinted, with a breathing dot, a polite live region, reading 'Finishing sign-in…' while redeeming. 'Open browser again' is a tonal secondary, first on Windows, then 'Cancel' and the quiet 'Use a code instead'.

Step 3: 'Choose a license' over 'DJDL will use it on Mara's PC.' Row anatomy, the same in every kit: the title is where the license came from ('Automatic grant', 'Key ending Q2KD7H') and never wraps, the tier is a pill, and the meta line is devices · duration ('2 of 5 devices · Lifetime'). The first license with a free device is preselected with a tint and one radio (no accent border). The full key row has no radio, 'No free devices · Lifetime' in the warning colour in the meta line's device slot (no tag on the title line) and 'Replace a device', and hides its counter and meter because the account holds a sign-in license (D-54).
Step 3 actions: 'Use a license key instead' as a quiet link, then 'Use this license and continue' and 'Cancel', primary first as on Windows.
After choosing an existing license there is no Done step: the form closes and the toast reads 'Signed in as Mara Fennick · Standard license'.

A visible 'Kit preview · fixture product' callout says DJDL really ships Swift and Kotlin and is drawn as an Electron build only to show the React kit inside the Electron kit (UK-06). The kit is product-agnostic.

Four sizes, and every window on the board takes one height, the tallest step's at that size, so a row's windows end and its captions start on one line. Wide draws three windows a row and the code completes the 3×3 (the art takes a third of a window under 720px, so the form keeps about 360px and the code never breaks); desktop puts the code in the head beside the lede and callout, so the eight windows fill four rows of two; tablet and phone put the code full width under the head; under 560px of window the art becomes a band above the form.

Failure states use the catalog's words in the same body: 'Can't reach Polaris Key' with Try again; 'This sign-in took too long' with Sign in again; 'Sign in with a code' with WDJB-MJHT, Copy, the countdown and no QR on desktop; and 'No DJDL license in this account', with the key field, Use another account and Get DJDL.

Board copy: the lede names what is drawn ('<PolarisKeyGate> in DJDL's Electron app on Windows.'); each caption is the state name plus at most one sentence the frame can't show; the fixture facts (sold on its own site, licenses through its groups, so nothing is created on 3b) are only in the callout; the code foot reads 'No theme set: the Polaris look in DJDL's accent. theme restyles it.' Step 1b opens no browser until Polaris Key answers, then Try again continues there; 2c draws no QR on a desktop.
Mockup kit v2 (B6, B7): weights 400/500/600, neutral annotation pins (gold means signing only), no glow; in-app kit frames keep the host or product accent as their primary (DL13).

Kit frames name Polaris Key only in the footnote (sdk-c-24): 'You're offline' for no network, 'Sign in in the window that opened' in the hand-off; the frames are DL v2 (product icon and name, one primary, the key as a quiet link, no 'or' divider) (site-35).

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the fixture is labelled where it is seen, rows lead with what tells them apart, button order is consistent, the header holds still, and the offline, expired, code and no-license states are drawn; the counter on the full key row stays hidden per D-54.

findings.issue: DJDL is drawn as an Electron app, though Integration and the CLI screens say it is Swift on macOS and Kotlin on Windows, and the fixture was acknowledged only in the JSON.
findings.resolution: Kept the Electron window and added a visible 'Kit preview · fixture product' callout to the intro. It says DJDL really ships Swift and Kotlin, and that it is drawn as an Electron build only to show the React kit inside the Electron kit (UK-06), with DJDL's own facts. The website alternative was declined because UK-06 is one of this screen's packages, and the Electron shell is where the loopback browser hand-off, the code view and the device choice all happen; a page on DJDL's site has none of them. The code panel's caption now says 'What the Electron build writes'.

findings.issue: In Choose a license, both rows are titled 'DJDL' with the same Standard pill, so the choices look identical until the third line.
findings.resolution: Each row now leads with what tells them apart, the origin: 'Automatic grant' (the access policy, the glossary's word) and 'Key ending Q2KD7H'. The meta line keeps only the term (Lifetime). Note for the lead: this refines SIGN-IN.md §3.6's row anatomy (title = license name, else product name) for rows that would share a title. sdk.swiftui-sign-in keeps license names because its tiers differ.

findings.issue: The button order flips: step 2 puts the primary first (Windows), but step 3 puts Cancel first.
findings.resolution: Step 3 now reads 'Use this license and continue' then 'Cancel', matching the Windows order in step 2, step 3b and the activation form.

findings.issue: Failure states the flow implies are never drawn: no license on this account, sign-in cancelled or expired, offline, and the body of 'Use a code instead'.
findings.resolution: Added four frames, worded from SIGN-IN.md and the kit catalog. 1b Offline: 'Can't reach Polaris Key' with Try again. 2b Sign-in didn't finish: drawn as 'This sign-in took too long' with Sign in again, and the caption gives the cancelled and browser-didn't-open wordings. 2c Use a code instead: 'Sign in with a code', key.plrs.im/device, WDJB-MJHT with Copy, the countdown, Open browser, Cancel and Use browser sign-in, with no QR on desktop. 3b 'No DJDL license in this account': 'Bought it with another email?', the key field with 'Add and use on this device', Use another account, Get DJDL ↗ and Cancel.

findings.issue: Step 2 makes 'Open browser again', a recovery action, the filled primary; and the row origin 'From signing in' is the word the glossary replaces with 'Automatic grant'.
findings.resolution: The waiting row is now the focus of step 2, tinted in DJDL's accent with strong text. Open browser again is a tonal secondary and Cancel a ghost button. SIGN-IN.md D-78 still calls Open browser again the primary, so the lead should update the spec. The picker uses 'Automatic grant', per integration.md §2 and the plan's recorded decision. The kit catalog's signin.choice.origin.signIn still reads 'From signing in', and packages/admin/src/portal/model/library.ts notes an owner polish that keeps it in the picker, so the lead should record which wins and update the catalog, both kits and the portal together.

findings.issue: The header moves between steps because each body is vertically centred, and the full key row hides its device counter, so 'No free devices' has no evidence.
findings.resolution: Applied: every body starts at a fixed 44px offset in a 640px window, so the icon and title sit at the same height on every step. Declined showing '5 of 5 devices' on the full key row: D-54 (SIGN-IN.md §3.6, carried in EXPERIENCE.md) hides a key license's counter and meter when the account also holds a sign-in license, and the 'No free devices' tag carries the fact. The SwiftUI Family row shows 5 of 5 because that account's other license is a Steam license, not a sign-in one. The step 3 caption says why.

findings.issue: Row 1's windows ended 20px apart at desktop and 16px at wide, because each window absorbed its caption's length.
findings.resolution: Every window on the board takes one height, the tallest step's at that size, and each figure is a two-row subgrid, so window bottoms and caption tops line up in every row (kit .frame-grid.windows). The Choose a license cuts shorten that tallest step. Rendered: all eight windows equal at each size.

findings.issue: At desktop the code panel sat alone in the last row beside about 650×430 of nothing, and about 580px beside the callout was empty too.
findings.resolution: 1280–1599: the board head is two columns (.board-head.split), the lede and fixture callout | 'What the Electron build writes', and the eight windows fill four rows of two. Tablet and phone: the code full width under the head. Wide: unchanged, the code completes the 3×3 (a .wide-only twin; the head's figure is .hide-wide).

findings.issue: Choose a license's title and lede both said 'this device'; the 'No free devices' tag forced 'Key ending / Q2KD7H' onto two lines at wide and phone.
findings.resolution: Title 'Choose a license' (lede 'DJDL will use it on Mara's PC.' stays). Row titles never wrap. On the full key row 'No free devices' moved to the meta line's device slot: 'No free devices · Lifetime' beside the Standard pill, in the warning colour. Catalog copy, so both kits follow it.

findings.issue: The lede, callout, captions and code foot repeated each other; captions ran two or three sentences of rationale with programme references; caption 4 pointed at a sidebar not drawn at tablet or phone; 1b's caption seemed to contradict Try again's ↗; 2b's second sentence repeated its button.
findings.resolution: Lede '<PolarisKeyGate> in DJDL's Electron app on Windows.' Each caption is the bold state name plus at most one sentence (1 'No logo row: DJDL has no provider connections. Have a license key? opens the key field in place.'; 1b 'No browser opens until Polaris Key answers; Try again then continues there.'; 3b 'Never a dead end: another account, a key, or buying DJDL.'; 4 'The account row is the kit's AccountAndLicense part.'). 'Morphs in place under a header that never moves', the live-region and breathing-dot rule, 'tonal' and D-54 are in the compare list; fixture facts only in the callout. 2b lede 'A sign-in link works for 10 minutes.' Code foot 'No theme set: the Polaris look in DJDL's accent. theme restyles it.'

findings.issue: Lower .kit-welcome's min-height to 480 so each window is sized to its content, and re-pair frames by height ([1,1b,2] [2b,2c,3b] [3,4,code] at wide) (ux1).
findings.resolution: declined: the app window doesn't resize between steps, and the kit's sign-in frames keep one header position with the foot at the bottom, so per-step heights would misdraw the product. The re-pairing also puts 3b before 3, out of story order. The empty band is reduced instead by one board-wide window height, taken from a shorter tallest step.

findings.issue: In 3b, order the actions as primary, then Use another account · Get DJDL, then Cancel last (d2).
findings.resolution: declined: the primary plus Cancel pair is the kit's button pair on every step (2, 2b, 2c, 3). Alternatives follow the pair, as 'Use a code instead' does on step 2. Splitting the pair in one step would break that consistency.

findings.issue: The desktop render opens on an unlabelled code block; windows have about 250px of dead space above the footer.
findings.resolution: One DOM order at every size (states 1 to 4, then the code card, full width, top-aligned, caption above it); windows take their row's tallest content height with the foot at the bottom (.windows.fit-rows); four windows per row at wide.

findings.issue: The privacy footer repeats in six windows; the code caption repeats the code's own comment.
findings.resolution: Footer only on the first sign-in window and the choose-a-license window; captions shortened as triaged; the code caption is "What the Electron build writes."; no subtitle; one-line kit-preview chip.

findings.issue: Hide states behind chips or use a scroll-snap strip on phone.
findings.resolution: declined: this removes content and adds interaction; windows are content-sized instead.

findings.issue: Delete the Signed in as toasts or shorten them to Signed in · Standard license.
findings.resolution: declined: the toast is a real product string, and the toast naming the account and license is the caption's point.
